incidents.title: Threat actors use ARTEX agents to search GitHub for OAuth application secrets and follow up
incidents.targets: Organizations whose OAuth application secrets were exposed in public repositories
incidents.outcome: Exposed OAuth application secrets were found and abused in follow-on attacks.
incidents.confidenceReason: Microsoft, which investigated the activity, states the actors used ARTEX agents.
incidents.summary: Actors used ARTEX agents to search GitHub repositories for OAuth application secrets, analyze what they found and carry out follow-on attacks with less hands-on-keyboard work. Microsoft notes it may overlap its other ARTEX reporting.
incidents.quote: However, agentic tooling like ARTEX allows threat actors to not only scan for secrets across multiple repositories at a quicker pace but also use the agents to analyze the output and conduct follow-on attacks, cutting down on the need for the threat actor to have hands-on-keyboard interactions throughout the attack chain.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Microsoft has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: BOSSAI operator coordinates AI agents to breach emergency-service and university systems
incidents.targets: Organizations across 11 countries; confirmed access or data theft at approximately 10 targets in Taiwan, Thailand and Mexico, including universities and emergency services
incidents.outcome: Confirmed system access and data theft, including medical information and personally identifiable information; many other targets were only scanned.
incidents.confidenceReason: Acronis examined the operator's agent conversations, commands, tools and victim data, directly linking AI agents to real intrusions.
incidents.summary: One operator manually coordinated 12 specialized agents, relying largely on locally hosted models with safeguards removed. Agents scanned systems and attempted exploitation, while the operator transferred findings between interfaces. The date records the disclosure month; the operation's start month is unspecified.
incidents.quote: So the attacks ran mainly on "abliterated" models: freely downloadable (open-weight) versions of DeepSeek, GLM and Qwen with their safety training removed.

incidents.title: CERT-In: AI-assisted actor CRAFTY FALCON escalates attacks on Indian BFSI payment and disbursement APIs
incidents.targets: Indian banking, payment, fintech and crypto entities (BFSI)
incidents.outcome: Escalating attacks on payment and disbursement APIs at Indian financial entities.
incidents.confidenceReason: CERT-In, a government body, states it found public AI offensive tools against the affected entities.
incidents.summary: CERT-In's advisories describe an AI-assisted actor it calls CRAFTY FALCON escalating attacks on payment and disbursement APIs in India's banking, financial services and insurance sector, with ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI found at affected entities.
incidents.quote: Analysis has identified the use of multiple publicly available AI-driven offensive security tools against affected entities including the "ARTEX" family of LLM-based, "PentAGI" autonomous multi-agent AI penetration testing system and the "Cairn" attack search engine, in addition to the "CyberStrikeAI" framework.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only CERT-In has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: CyberStrikeAI framework automates post-exploitation against educational institutions

incidents.outcome: Domain admin was reached within three to four days of agent deployment in one case.
incidents.confidenceReason: Kaspersky, which analyzed the intrusions, states the framework's LLM planned and generated the commands.

incidents.quote: The first step involves deploying the CyberStrikeAI C2 agent, which receives commands from a server-based LLM orchestrator.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Kaspersky has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: Operation Snowball uses a DeepSeek agent against a European telecom provider
incidents.nexus: Chinese-language operator indicators; no established state attribution
incidents.targets: An unnamed European telecommunications provider and 13 associated organizations
incidents.outcome: Transcripts reportedly document compromises and potential access to patient records, credentials and private keys; reported extraction has not been independently confirmed.
incidents.confidenceReason: SC Media relays Infosecurity's report of what Malbear Labs, the investigator, found. Malbear Labs' own report has not been found; with it, the grade could be Confirmed.
incidents.summary: A custom agent operated for more than two weeks with high-level instructions from a Chinese-speaking operator. It adapted exploitation and tunneling attempts when blocked and created replacement tools. The date records the reporting month because the supplied material does not establish the operation's start month.
incidents.quote: While the operator provided high-level instructions in Chinese, the AI handled the technical execution, including the creation of replacement tools.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only SC Media has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: DOJ SDNY indicts three over AI voice and image impersonation of executives and lawyers that cost companies $129M
incidents.actor: Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, Guy Sheetrit and co-conspirators (charged)
incidents.outcome: Companies lost about $129 million in wire transfers, per the charges.
incidents.confidenceReason: Federal prosecutors allege the AI use in an indictment; these are charges, not findings.
incidents.summary: Prosecutors in the Southern District of New York charged three men with using AI to mimic executives' voices and images and to impersonate attorneys on calls, inducing employees to wire about $129 million. The scheme ran from about July 2024 to February 2026.
incidents.quote: According to the Indictment:(1) Between 2024 and 2026, SOALL, HAZAN, SHEETRIT, and their co-conspirators used SI to impersonate the voices and/or images of corporate executives at numerous companies (the “Victim Companies”) and attorneys at major law firms in order to trick employees into sending large payments to bank accounts all over the world controlled by members of the conspiracy.

incidents.title: Strix operator repeatedly compromises a gambling platform's admin backend
incidents.targets: Gambling websites, including one platform's administrative backend
incidents.outcome: Administrative access persisted for approximately two weeks; the operation regained access four times before losing it permanently.
incidents.confidenceReason: Coalition inspected exposed operator material documenting model switching, successful compromise and repeated access checks.
incidents.summary: The operator cycled among DeepSeek, Gemini and GLM to overcome refusals, then used Strix with exploits and stolen credentials against a gambling platform. Coalition recorded 2,968 health checks. The date records the disclosure month; attack dates were not specified.
incidents.quote: After finding a compliant model, the operator managed to compromise a gambling platform's admin backend for about two weeks, using both software exploits and stolen credentials.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Coalition has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.
